items.title: Flames takeaways: Rookie Jonathan Castagna hits milestone in win
items.summary: Jonathan Castagna stole the show on Tuesday with his first two NHL goals, which were key to the Flames’ second win in three California road games.
items.body: On any other night, stripping Macklin Celebrini from a pretty good scoring opportunity would have been a highlight for Jonathan Castagna . But it paled in comparison to the fact he finished the night with the first two goals of his NHL career. “I’m really grateful for the opportunity in the first place,” the rookie centre told Sportsnet’s Brendan Parker following the Flames’ 5-2 win in San Jose. “To score a goal in this league is a really special moment. It’s been a long time coming. There have been a lot of chances I wish I could have back.” Castagna, who was acquired last season in the MacKenzie Weegar deal, was called up early from the Wranglers this season and has made it clear with his 200-foot game he isn’t going back. He extended the Flames lead to 4-1 early in the third when he fought his way to the front of the net and turned to bat in an Aydar Suniev rebound out of the air to kickstart a celebration that saw his teammates shower him with water as he did his fly-by. “They were spraying me with water pretty good — I was trying not to smile, and keep it cool, but it was a pretty special moment and I was smiling ear-to-ear,” said the Toronto native. “It’s really nice to finally get one in the back of the net, but also see the reaction from the guys being like that — it’s heartwarming.” With the net empty, and things getting chippy, Castagna batted in another one after Martin Pospisil did his best to ensure he got the puck to the popular young centre who swept it in. On a night when Pospisil and Matt Coronato scored to put the Flames up 2-1 in the first period, it was Castagna and another Flame who stole the show with milestone moments that were key to the team’s second win in three California road games. items.title: Gauthier stays red-hot, 'playing with a lot of confidence' for Ducks
items.summary: ST. LOUIS -- Cutter Gauthier hears all the noise and sees all the headlines.
items.body: 22-year-old forward extends goal streak to 10 games with fourth hat trick of season in loss to Blues ST. LOUIS -- Cutter Gauthier hears all the noise and sees all the headlines. So, the Anaheim Ducks forward is doing his best to adopt tunnel vision as he continues to score goals at a record pace. That was evident again on Tuesday, when he extended his goal streak to 10 games by getting a hat trick, his fourth during the run, in an 8-6 loss to the St. Louis Blues at Enterprise Center. ANA@STL: Gauthier records his fourth hat trick of the season and fifth of his career The 22-year-old, who also had an assist in the loss, has 19 goals during the streak, which is one game shy of tying Teemu Selanne (Oct. 21 to Nov. 10, 1997) for the longest in Ducks history. He's also the third player in NHL history to have a goal streak of at least 10 games before the age of 23, joining Babe Dye (11 games in 1920-21) and Mike Bossy (10 games in 1978-79). "It obviously gets published a lot what’s going on, but if I let the online chats and stuff, the pressure and all that stuff, get to me, it’s not going to be good," Gauthier told NHL.com. "When I play at my best, I’m playing free. I’m not thinking, I’m just flowing, I’m using my instincts and being great. I don’t let that affect me. I haven’t these last handful of weeks, so I’m going to keep that going." Gauthier certainly hasn't let it affect him, considering he has 24 points (19 goals, five assists) during an NHL career-high 12-game point streak. He also has 21 goals in 21 games this season, which is tied with Leon Draisaitl of the Edmonton Oilers for the NHL lead. Another blown lead. Another missed opportunity. Another regulation loss. Getting on the road…. The urgency to snap a six-game losing skid…. Alas, Sergei Bobrovsky gave up a touchdown (plus an extra point, called back due to video review) in his 11th loss and Toronto's ninth in regulation over its past 10 attempts. The Leafs found fresh ways to stunt their momentum, allowing Chicago to strike back 35 seconds and 12 seconds, respectively, after their second- and third-period comeback goals. And the head man inside those visitors' coaching quarters boarded a plane home more disappointed than usual. “I’m disappointed tonight,” Jim Hiller said. “I’m disappointed every night. items.body: Forward to see time defending Suzuki, type of responsibility captain welcomes NEWARK, N.J. -- Nico Hischier knows his most important contribution for the New Jersey Devils won't always appear on the score sheet. That might be winning a defensive-zone face-off, staying above the puck instead of joining the rush or sacrificing an offensive opportunity to remain on the proper side of an opposing star. Those details will again be critical when the Devils host the Montreal Canadiens at Prudential Center for NHL on Prime "Wednesday Night Hockey" (7:30 p.m. ET; MSGSN, Prime). The Devils captain likely will spend significant time against Canadiens captain Nick Suzuki , who has 17 points (eight goals, nine assists) in 15 games while winning 55.4 percent of his face-offs. Suzuki's intelligence, patience with the puck and chemistry with Cole Caufield , who leads Montreal with 12 goals in 21 games, will test Hischier's positioning and awareness. "I view it as part of my game I want to play, and I take that as my job that game, and it contributes to the team," Hischier said. "I obviously take pride in that. If you're able to shut down a good line, then you give your team a chance to win a hockey game." Those assignments, combined with Hischier's production on offense and leadership as captain, have earned him respect throughout the NHL and inside New Jersey's dressing room. "He goes about the game and his business the right way," linemate Luke Evangelista said. "He's an honest player, works his hardest every night, plays a responsible 200-foot game. Blackhawks coach Jeff Blashill said he’d have more of an update on Wednesday, after the captain had further testing done. Bedard was setting up to take a face-off against Toronto forward Nick Paul 54 seconds into the third period when Paul’s stick made contact with Bedard’s right hand. The Blackhawks captain yelled out in pain and immediately went to the locker room. “It looked what it looked like. I hate to comment further until I know more,” Blashill said. “I think everybody saw it, so you can certainly draw your own conclusions. I don’t know what that means though, so I don’t want to speak about it. Just know we’ll get further testing done and we’ll have a better update. Just don’t want to talk without knowing for sure.” The 21-year-old leads the Blackhawks with 18 points (seven goals, 11 assists) in 15 games. He scored his seventh goal of the season at 18:51 of the second period on Tuesday, and the Blackhawks didn’t let up after that. The Blackhawks, who lost seven of their past eight entering Tuesday’s game, felt some motivation to win this one for Bedard. “When he’s in the lineup, he brings a certain amount of intensity that we all feed off. Kirill Kaprizov had three assists to reach 40 points on the season. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Matthew Schaefer can’t stop making history. The New York Islanders’ defenseman scored a hat trick during the team’s 5-1 win over the Columbus Blue Jackets Tuesday night, becoming the third teenage defenseman in NHL history to record three goals in a game. The other two teenage defenders to achieve the feat were Phil Housley and Hannu Virta, both with the Buffalo Sabres during the 1982-83 season. Schaefer, 19, finished the night with three goals and nine shots in 23:23 of ice time. The Islanders are now 10-6-4 with 24 points this season. Through 20 games in 2026-27, Schaefer has nine goals and 15 assists for 24 points, averaging 26:58 of ice time per game. The Hamilton, Ont., native has 32 goals and 51 assists for 83 points in 102 career NHL contests. Schaefer is coming off one of the most impressive seasons for a rookie defenseman in NHL history. He finished with 23 goals and 36 assists for 59 points, averaged 24:41 of ice time per game, capped off by winning the 2026 Calder Trophy for rookie of the year . His 23 goals placed him second among all NHL defenseman in 2025-26, behind only Jakob Chychrun of the Washington Capitals . He made NHL history by tying Hockey Hall of Famer Brian Leetch for the most goals by a rookie defender , and also became the youngest blueliner in NHL history to reach 50 points in a season . Schaefer was selected by the Islanders with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2025 NHL Entry Draft, despite the fact he played just 73 career OHL regular-season games due to injuries. In parts of two seasons with the Erie Otters, the 6-foot-2 defender posted 10 goals and 29 assists for 39 points.

items.body: The Chicago Blackhawks captain could be staring down another injury. Connor Bedard exited Tuesday's game against the Toronto Maple Leafs early in the third period after appearing to suffer an injury off a face-off. Bedard appeared to be in immediate pain after the draw and headed off the ice and to the dressing room, favouring his right arm. He did not return to the game, which the Blackhawks won 6-3. After the game, head coach Jeff Blashill had no concrete update and said that Bedard will undergo more testing on Wednesday that will give the team a better idea on the extent of his injury. "It looked like what it looked like," Blashill told reporters . "I hate to comment further until I know more." The 21-year-old has a history of shoulder injuries, missing extended time last season with a right shoulder injury and undergoing surgery on his left shoulder in the off-season. Bedard missed the first five Blackhawks games of the season as he rehabbed the injury. Prior to exiting on Tuesday, Bedard scored Chicago's go-ahead goal. items.body: SUNRISE, Fla. — Connor McDavid had a goal and an assist to extend his season-opening points streak to 23 games, and the Edmonton Oilers continued their sizzling start by beating the rival Florida Panthers 5-2 on Tuesday night. McDavid now has 13 goals and 42 assists, and the 23-game streak to start a season ties Wayne Gretzky for the fifth-longest in NHL history. Only Gretzky (51- and 30-game streaks), Quebec's Mats Sundin (30) and Pittsburgh's Mario Lemieux (28) had longer streaks to open a season. Vasily Podkolzin scored twice, while Kasperi Kapanen and Leon Draisaitl each had a goal and two assists for Edmonton, which lost the 2024 and 2025 Stanley Cup finals to Florida. Devon Levi got the win in net for the Oilers, improving to 10-1-0 on the season. Matthew Tkachuk scored twice in the third period for Florida, which trailed 4-0 entering the final minutes. It was his first multi-goal game of the season. Edmonton (17-3-3) won its sixth straight and has 37 points through 23 games, tying for the second-most in team history. The 55 points through 23 games have McDavid in elite company. Only two other players — Gretzky and Lemieux, both doing it on three occasions — have managed that many points this quickly into a season. Lemieux was the last to do it, posting 66 points through 23 games in 1995-96. The Panthers were again without forwards Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand, who have both been sidelined for all but two games of the season. Panthers coach Paul Maurice said both are expected to meet with physicians later this week, an indicator that their returns to the lineup could be looming.

Pittsburgh couldn’t send him there without his approval. The report confirms a rumor from last week. On Spittin’ Chiclets , former NHL defenseman Keith Yandle said he’d heard Rakell turned down a trade to Chicago and that Rutger McGroarty was recalled from the AHL in case the deal went through. It’s easy to see why Chicago was interested. LeBrun reported earlier this month that the Blackhawks hoped to add a scoring winger but were “not too picky” given how hard it is to make trades this early in the season. Through 12 games, Chicago had just eight points and the league’s second-worst points percentage. It ranked 31st in goals per game and power-play percentage. Rakell, 33, has six goals and five assists in 20 games this season. He had 24 goals and 24 assists in 60 games a year ago and posted a career-high 70 points in 2024-25. His 35 goals that season led the Penguins. He signed a six-year, $30MM contract with Pittsburgh on July 11, 2022. The deal carries a $5MM cap hit and runs through the 2027-28 season. His eight-team no-trade list covers the full length of the contract. Rakell should stay on the market. He is one of several Penguins who could be traded before the March 1 deadline, with Pittsburgh projected to sell. items.body: Explanation: The play on the ice was challenged under Rule 38 – Coach’s Challenge. Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. If a review is not conclusive and/or there is any doubt whatsoever as to whether the call on the ice was correct, the original call on the ice will be confirmed.” Video review determined Ottawa’s Fabian Zetterlund’s presence and contact in the crease impaired Stuart Skinner’s ability to play his position prior to Dylan Cozen’s goal. The decision was made in accordance with Rule 69.1 which states, in part, “Goals should be disallowed only if: (1) an attacking player, either by his positioning or by contact, impairs the goalkeeper’s ability to move freely within his crease or defend his goal.”

items.title: Flames’ Sam Honzek out week-to-week with wrist injury
items.summary: Honzek suffered a wrist injury during an AHL game over the weekend. It was his first game since he missed a month with a separate injury.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Sergei Belski-Imagn Images The Calgary Wranglers , the AHL affiliate for the Calgary Flames , announced Tuesday that forward Sam Honzek will be out week-to-week with a wrist injury. Honzek, 22, suffered the injury during the Wranglers’ game against the Henderson Silver Knights Saturday night. It was his first AHL game of 2026-27 after he missed more than a month with a lower-body injury he suffered during an NHL game in early October against the Colorado Avalanche . In 27 career NHL contests, Honzek, a native of Trencin, Slovakia, has two goals and two assists for four points. He also has eight goals and 13 assists for 21 points in 55 career AHL regular-season games. Honzek was taken in the first round of the 2023 NHL Entry Draft (No. 16 overall). He spent two seasons playing junior hockey with the Western Hockey League’s Vancouver Giants where he scored 33 goals and 54 assists for 87 points in 76 games. Internationally, Honzek has represented his native Slovakia on numerous occasions, including three appearances at the World Junior Championships between 2022 and 2024. He also played for them at the 2025 World Championship. The Flames are 9-11-1 with 19 points through 21 games in 2026-27. They are sixth in the Pacific Division and four points back of the second Wild Card spot in the Western Conference. Calgary is on the road and will face the San Jose Sharks at SAP Center on Tuesday night.

items.title: Oilers’ McDavid extends point streak to hit historic milestone
items.body: Connor McDavid 's record-setting season continues as he joins more elite company. The forward is now tied for the third longest points streak to start the season in NHL history, as he reached 23 games with his 13th goal of the season against the Florida Panthers on Tuesday. McDavid ties Wayne Gretzky's 1988-89 streak with his first power-play goal of the season. He sits behind Mats Sundin in 1992-93 (30) and Gretzky in 1982-82 (30), as well as Gretzky in 1983-84 (51) for longest to start a season. items.body: Olczyk, Savard, Roenick, Chelios and Foley discuss historic 100-year anniversary for franchise CHICAGO – It’s been 100 years for the Chicago Blackhawks, and they wrapped up their Centennial celebration prior to their game against the Toronto Maple Leafs on Tuesday. Along with a one-night-only exhibit featuring rare artifacts, historic memorabilia and photography in the atrium section of United Center, the Blackhawks had all five of their ambassadors take part in a Q&A about 90 minutes before the game: former forwards Eddie Olczyk , Denis Savard and Jeremy Roenick , former defenseman Chris Chelios and former play-by-play broadcaster Pat Foley. Tuesday marked the 100th anniversary of the first game in Blackhawks history, a 4-1 win against the Toronto St. Patricks on Nov. 17, 1926. “Pat, what was the traffic like getting to that first game?” Olczyk said to Foley. Olczyk was Foley’s broadcast partner with the Blackhawks from 2006-22. The five talked for about 20 minutes about the history of the Blackhawks, including the old Chicago Stadium, where the team played from 1929-94. all smiles when you get this squad together 😂❤️ pic.twitter.com/BpLn2ztJGs “(Nothing like it), especially growing up here in Chicago as a fan and being in the crowd,” said Chelios, who was traded from the Montreal Canadiens to his hometown Blackhawks for Savard on June 29, 1990. “That’s really the only reason why I knew what to expect when I got traded here.” “To walk up those stairs, hear the crowd that brought out sometimes the best, sometimes the worst, but anybody playing against us knew they were up for war. It was the toughest place to play for the opposition. The fans were great; it was smoke filled in the rafters. Those old buildings, but especially old Chicago stadium, I loved playing there.”

items.body: Register Login Kiefer Sherwood Out Week-To-Week By Ryan Long | at November 17, 2026 6:47 pm Sharks winger Kiefer Sherwood is considered week-to-week with an upper-body injury, head coach Ryan Warsofsky told reporters Tuesday, via Curtis Pashelka of the Bay Area News Group . Sherwood won’t require surgery, but there is no definitive timeline for his return. Sherwood got hurt in the third period of Sunday’s 4-2 win over the Predators. Nashville defenseman Jayden Struble shoved him awkwardly into the boards, and he was favoring his right arm and shoulder as he left the ice. His right arm was in a sling as he left the locker room after the game. He finished with two shots and two hits in 10:55 of ice time. “He was playing some good hockey for us and is a very valuable piece,” Warsofsky said. He also called the injury another opportunity for other players to step up. San Jose will likely miss Sherwood most on the forecheck. Warsofsky said Sherwood “just disrupts and gets a stick on a lot of pucks.” To fill the roster spot, the Sharks recalled veteran forward Brett Leason from the AHL’s San Jose Barracuda. Leason made the team out of training camp but hasn’t played this season. Sherwood, 31, has two goals and six assists in 23 games this season, and he leads the NHL with 115 hits. Last season, between Vancouver and San Jose, he had 23 goals and 13 assists in 72 games with 339 hits. A season earlier, he set the NHL single-season record with 462 hits and posted career highs with 19 goals and 40 points in 78 games for the Canucks. items.body: Fresh off gold medal at IIHF Worlds, Olympic champion continues to inspire kids, grow game Laila Edwards and Ice Hockey in Harlem are having quite the week. Edwards won a gold medal with the United States Women’s National Team at the 2026 IIHF Women’s World Championship, defeating Canada 6-2 in Herning, Denmark, on Monday for back-to-back titles for the first time since 2016 sandwiched between winning gold at the 2026 Winter Olympics. The 22-year-old defenseman from Cleveland Heights, Ohio, also won $23,000 on a prerecorded episode of FOX’s “Celebrity Name That Tune” on Monday. She made a special appearance at the 2026 NHL Draft in Buffalo and announced the San Jose Sharks' selection of forward Ivar Stenberg with the No. 2 pick. She joined fellow Team USA women's and men's hockey players on an episode of "Celebrity Family Feud" that aired in July. Edwards was selected with the fourth pick in the 2026 Professional Women's Hockey League by the expansion San Jose Sea Lions in June and signed a three-year contract on Sept. 14. Mantha is projected to be out for a month, though the exact timeline remains uncertain. “The way it’s described to me, it’s going to be a tricky one, because it’s a very rare injury for any athlete, really,” Keefe said . “So it’s just more so about when he’ll be ready to take contact again, and they’re going to feel that out. “But he’ll be back on skates relatively soon. With 7:25 to go in the third period, Mantha was scrambling for the puck at the Isles netfront when defenseman Adam Pelech high-sticked him in the throat. items.title: Scheifele rewriting record books of resurgent Winnipeg Jets
items.summary: Mark Scheifele is well on his way to rewriting the Winnipeg Jets’ record books.
items.body: Mark Scheifele is well on his way to rewriting the Winnipeg Jets ' record books. Leading the comeback with a four-point effort and the shootout winner over the Chicago Blackhawks on Saturday, Scheifele passed his mentor Dale Hawerchuk for most career points in franchise history with 933. With three helpers in the game, he also eclipsed Thomas Steen for the club mark in assists. Scheifele needs just one more goal to pass Hawerchuk for first, with both sitting at 379. "Honestly, it's pretty incredible," Scheifele said after the game. "You'd never thought I'd be here, but honestly, just so blessed to play with the players that I played with over my career. Blake Wheeler, Kyle Connor, Josh Morrissey, Dustin Byfuglien, Andrew Ladd, Bryan Little ... I wouldn't be there without all those guys, and just very blessed." The milestone carried some added weight, as the history-making coincided with the Jets' mentors trip. Shifting from the traditional "dad's trip," every player got to invite a male mentor on Winnipeg's two-game road swing through Dallas and Chicago. Scheifele, whose father, Brad, died of cancer in May 2025, invited Gregg Derlago, his billet dad during his early years in Winnipeg. Derlago had given Scheifele a pin with a picture of him and his dad when he was younger, which he wore after the game while being interviewed by reporters. "He's up there watching, and Dale's up there watching as well," Scheifele said. "Pretty special to do this tonight with all the mentors here. To get to experience that with all of them is honestly something I'll remember forever." While Scheifele basked in the moment thanks to the comeback win, the absence of two major male figures in his life loomed large. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: PWHL On Tuesday, the Vancouver Goldeneyes announced that goaltender E merance Maschmeyer is taking a leave of absence from the team to attend to a personal, private matter. For roster management purposes, Maschemeyer is going to be placed on long-term injured reserve, as of Dec. 3, when roster compliance must begin. In a statement, Goldeneyes general manager Alison Izzi says that the organization is behind the veteran netminder. “We fully support Emerance’s decision to step away from hockey at this time to focus on a private personal matter,” Izzi said. “Our priority is ensuring she has the time and space she needs. Out of respect for Emerance, we will have no further comment at this time and ask that her privacy be respected. We will provide updates on her status when appropriate.” Maschmeyer was Vancouver’s starter during its inaugural season. She posted a 7-9-2-0 record, with a 2.57 goals-against average, a .916 save percentage and one shutout. Her performance was impressive, given how tough of a first season it was for the expansion Goldeneyes, who finished sixth in the PWHL, but ultimately earned enough Gold Plan points to win the first-overall pick. The Bruderheim, Alta. native signed with the Goldeneyes after spending the first two years of the PWHL with the Ottawa Charge. In 60 career games, Maschmeyer has a record of 22-25-8-2, with a 2.47 GAA, a .915 SV% and three shutouts. items.title: Mantha, Kovacevic out at least one month for Devils
items.summary: Anthony Mantha and Johnathan Kovacevic will be out for an extended period, New Jersey Devils coach Sheldon Keefe said on Tuesday.
items.body: Forward sustained fractured throat, defenseman has high ankle sprain Anthony Mantha and Johnathan Kovacevic will be out for an extended period, New Jersey Devils coach Sheldon Keefe said on Tuesday. Mantha is projected to be out one month after the forward had surgery Monday to repair a fracture in his throat. He was injured in a 5-4 overtime win at the New York Islanders on Nov. 7 but should be able to resume skating in the near future. However, it’s uncertain when Mantha will be able to return. The Devils will need to evaluate when Mantha can safely withstand contact because of the unusual nature of the injury. "That one, I guess, from the way it's described to me, is going to be a tricky one because it's a very rare injury for any athlete, really," Keefe said. "So, it's just more so about when he'll be ready to take contact again, and they're going to feel that out." Kovacevic, a defenseman, is expected to miss 4-6 weeks because of a high ankle sprain he sustained in a 5-2 loss at the Winnipeg Jets on Nov. 10. He has two assists in 13 games and averages 14:40 of ice time. Brett Pesce (illness), however, was a full participant at practice Tuesday and is expected to return against the Montreal Canadiens at Prudential Center in Newark, New Jersey, on Wednesday (7:30 p.m. ET; MSGSN, Prime). The defenseman missed two games. Seamus Casey took another step in his recovery by skating on his own Tuesday. However, Keefe said he had not received an updated timetable for when the defenseman can play. Casey had knee surgery at the beginning of October after being injured during a preseason game at the New York Rangers on Sept. 24. The initial timeline for his recovery was 8-10 weeks.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: (Steven Ellis/The Nation Network) The St. Louis Blues announced Tuesday that forward Adam Jecho has been cleared through the NHL/NHLPA Player Assistance Program and will rejoin the organization. The team said Jecho has been assigned to the Springfield Thunderbirds, their American Hockey League affiliate, and will report immediately. The league announced in September that Jecho would receive care from the player assistance program. A native of Zlin, Czechia, Jecho was taken No. 95 overall in the third round of the 2024 NHL Entry Draft. He signed a three-year, entry-level contract with the Blues that kicked in this season and will last through the 2028-29 campaign. The 6-foot-5 center spent three seasons with the Western Hockey League’s Edmonton Oil Kings, where he scored 58 goals and added 78 assists for 136 points in 157 career regular-season games. His best season came in 2024-25 where he recorded 25 goals and 28 assists for 53 points in 56 games. Going into Tuesday, the Blues are 9-9-2 with 20 points through their first 20 games of the 2026-27 regular season. They are seventh in the Central Division and three points back of the second Wildcard spot in the Western Conference. The Blues have a three-way tie for the team lead in points , with forwards Jimmy Snuggerud, Dylan Holloway and Robert Thomas all having 14 points. Snuggerud, 22, leads the team with 10 goals while Thomas leads with 11 assists. Philip Broberg leads all defenders with four goals and nine assists for 13 points and is averaging a team-high 24:33 of ice time per game.

Would he play again? Would the pain return? Would he ever be the same player? And, perhaps most importantly, would he be able to enjoy a normal life without constantly wondering what his hip had in store for him? “I think it's just ups and downs,” Huberdeau said, describing the mental gymnastics of an eight-month rehabilitation following surgery. “Are you gonna come back, or are you gonna be as good as before? Better than before? Not as good? There was some point that I was hurting a lot, and you're like, ‘OK, well, is it gonna be like this for the rest of my life?” Devin Cooley, the Flames' resident philosopher, certainly has a gift for putting things in perspective. Whatever the secret, Huberdeau is finally ready to put the uncertainty behind him and get back to playing hockey. The 33-year-old Flames winger will make his long-awaited return to game action Wednesday night at the Saddledome when he suits up for the Calgary Wranglers on an injury conditioning loan that represents the biggest milestone yet in his comeback from surgery last March. Eight months after going under the knife, he's nervous, excited and understandably eager to find out what happens when the puck drops. “I mean, I haven't played for a while. I think that's just a normal part. items.body: The New Jersey Devils are down two players for the next while. That Nov. 3 win has galvanized the Jets, who have won six in a row, including erasing another four-goal deficit Saturday against the Chicago Blackhawks. (Winnipeg became the second team in NHL history with multiple four-goal comeback wins over a six-game span.) “To see the character in this room that there’s no giving up, there’s always fight and especially at a time when we lost a bunch in a row and it’s really easy to lay your gloves down and be done and move on to the next one, to see the team keep fighting and get that win (against the Canadiens), it’s almost impossible not to get a spark out of that,” Jets centre and new franchise points leader Mark Scheifele told reporters . items.summary: The 33-year-old is likely to make his return on Tuesday against the Coachella Valley Firebirds.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Calgary Flames forward Jonathan Huberdeau is making his way back to competitive hockey, but will begin his comeback with a conditioning stint with the AHL’s Calgary Wranglers, who share the Scotiabank Saddledome with the NHL club. Under the terms of the CBA, a player who has been out with a long-term injury, defined as missing at least 24 days and 10 games, can be sent to the AHL on a conditioning loan. The loan is limited to three games or six games, whichever is longer, but can be extended by two additional games at request. While he is with the Wranglers, Huberdeau won’t count towards Calgary’s active NHL roster, but will count towards the NHL salary cap. The 33-year-old Huberdeau underwent hip surgery in the spring and has not played a competitive game since Feb. 4, when he scored in a 4-3 Flames win over the Edmonton Oilers . Before his injury, he posted 10 goals and 15 assists in 50 games with the Flames, bringing his NHL career totals to 263 goals, 544 assists and 807 points in 962 games since making his debut with the Florida Panthers in the 2012-13 season. “I’m feeling pretty good. It’s a big surgery,” Huberdeau said in September. “There’s no pain anymore, which is nice to deal with. Just now, the goal is to come back and be 100%.” Now with the Wranglers, he could return at home on Tuesday and Wednesday night against the Coachella Valley Firebirds, before the team heads on the road to take on the Laval Rocket on Saturday and Sunday. If his recovery and form-building remain on track, he could be with the Flames as soon as next week, as they enjoy a mediocre start to the 2026-27 season, with 19 points in their first 21 games and four short of the final Wild Card spot in the Western Conference.

items.body: The legacy of Johnny and Matthew Gaudreau is set to be recognized in their home state of New Jersey. The Gaudreau Brothers Inspiration Sculpture is to be built outside Hollydell Ice Arena in Sewell, N.J., where they grew up playing, the NHL announced on Tuesday. The statue is expected to be unveiled in the spring of 2028. The bronze sculpture, designed by New Jersey-based artist Carl LeVotch, will stand five-foot-nine. LeVotch is aiming for the statue to recognize the "humility, kindness, family devotion, perseverance and sportsmanship" that defined the Gaudreaus' lives. LeVotch is working with the Gaudreau Brothers Sculpture Project, a non-profit organization, to help fund the design. Before the crash that claimed the lives of both brothers on Aug. 29, 2024, Johnny had completed 11 NHL seasons in which he recorded 243 goals and 500 assists for 743 points across 763 games with the Calgary Flames and Columbus Blue Jackets. Matthew Gaudreau logged 105 points over four seasons in the ECHL and AHL after graduating from Boston College in 2017.

items.summary: Levi’s breakout could change Edmonton’s trajectory not just this season but in seasons to come.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Nov 14, 2026; Toronto, Ontario, CAN; Edmonton Oilers goalie Devon Levi (27) relaxes during warmup before playing the Toronto Maple Leafs at Scotiabank Arena. Mandatory Credit: Dan Hamilton-Imagn Images What do you want the goalie on your favorite NHL team to be thinking while he protects a lead in the final seconds of a game? It’s tough to imagine a more inspiring mantra than what Devon Levi uttered to himself with 10 seconds left on the clock Saturday night and superstar Auston Matthews poised to fire a backhander from the slot. Levi didn’t flinch or quake or shrink in his crease as he stared down the Toronto Maple Leafs captain. Levi met the challenge with a smile and battled through a flurry of desperate chances as his Edmonton Oilers held on for a 1-0 road win at Scotiabank Arena. It marked the first shutout of Levi’s NHL career, and it improved his record to 9-1-0 in what has been a stellar start to his 2026-27 season. After the game, Levi, 24, beamed with pride as he spoke to reporters and recounted his inner monologue during that climactic scramble. He wore the expression of a young man whose dreams were coming true but also someone who appreciates how unlikely the moment seemed even half a year earlier. As recently as last season, Levi existed in a purgatory somewhere between a prospect sure to become an impactful NHLer and “It would’ve happened by now.” Acquired as the centerpiece to the Buffalo Sabres’ trade of Sam Reinhart to the Florida Panthers in 2021, Levi was considered a borderline can’t-miss star in his late teens to early 20s. He posted a jaw-dropping .964 save percentage for Canada at the 2021 World Juniors. He won the Mike Richter Award as NCAA Div. I’s top goaltender in 2021-22 and 2022-23 playing for Northeastern.

As proud as we are of the players they became, we are even prouder of the people they were: kind, humble and devoted to their families and everyone around them. Of course, we don’t know what the plan is — or was — because NHL teams at the bottom of the standings do not ordinarily clutter their active roster with a third goalie, but Tolopilo’s first game for the Canucks since last season should earn him a longer stay. Stanley Cup contenders, the Knights are a heavy, physical team. The Mammoth are pretty heavy, too, but with considerably more speed and youth. items.body: SALT LAKE CITY — Brock Boeser scored a power-play goal with 4:23 left to lift the Vancouver Canucks to a 3-2 victory over the Utah Mammoth on Monday night. Jake DeBrusk flicked the puck out to Boeser and he threaded it inside the post to help Vancouver win consecutive games for the first time this season. DeBrusk and Filip Chytil also scored goals for the Canucks. Nikita Tolopilo made 32 saves in his season debut for Vancouver. Vincent Trocheck and Barrett Hayton scored for Utah, which lost is sixth straight game. Karel Vejmelka had 21 stops for the Mammoth. Neither team found the net until DeBrusk chipped in a power-play goal at the post with 4:55 left in the second. Vancouver scored 10 seconds into the power play after Boeser crossed the puck into DeBrusk while he battled Lawson Crouse for position at the post. Trocheck got Utah on the board at 2:51 of the third, snapping in the puck on a power play. The Canucks regained the lead on Chytil’s goal at 4:40 of the third. Chytil drew Vejmelka out to the post, wrapped around the net, and deflected the puck off the goaltender’s heel for the easy goal. Hayton leveled the score again with 8:20 left, snapping the puck over Tolopilo’s shoulder.

Today, we look at the race for the Norris Trophy , awarded annually to the top defenseman in the NHL as selected in a vote by the Professional Hockey Writers Association. Evan Bouchard started the season fast and hasn't slowed down since. The Edmonton Oilers defenseman had five points, including a hat trick, in a season-opening 6-5 overtime loss to the Vancouver Canucks on Sept. 29, and has been scoring ever since. He had a goal and two assists in his second game, and has 11 multipoint games this season. Bouchard is fourth in the NHL with 36 points, and leads defenseman with 12 goals. "I think things are just clicking right now, I feel good out there," Bouchard said recently. "Usually when the team plays well, individuals have success and that's what's happening right now. We're all playing as a team and it's working out for everyone." "Well, I didn't know he was this good, this talented, saw this many plays, moved the puck as good as he does," said Mike Babcock, who was named Oilers coach June 23. "… There's no question he should be in the running for the Norris (Trophy) every year. He's that good. We've just got to get him to be a little more competitive defensively, and he's already working towards that, and then he'll be right at the front of that group." Connor McDavid is off to the best start of his illustrious NHL career for the Edmonton Oilers, and his advanced metrics are fueling what could be one of the highest-scoring seasons in history. McDavid has points in each of his 22 games this season, tied with Dany Heatley (22 games in 2005-06) for the fifth-longest season-opening point streak in League history. McDavid also matched Gretzky (22 games in 1984-85) as the fastest player ever to reach 40 assists in a season; Gretzky (four times) and Lemieux (two times) are the only players other than McDavid to record 40 assists in 25 games or fewer. This season, McDavid leads the NHL in two-point games (14), three-point games (nine; four more than all others) and four-point games (five; three more than all others). The 29-year-old is on pace for 202 points in 84 games, which would challenge Gretzky's current single-season scoring record (215 in 1985-86). items.title: Canadiens give up three unanswered goals in loss to Rangers
items.body: NEW YORK — Will Cuylle scored twice, including the go-ahead short-handed goal in the final minute of the second period, and the New York Rangers rallied to defeat the Montreal Canadiens 3-1 on Monday night. The Rangers have won three in a row and six of their past seven and improved to 9-2-0 at home. Their latest victory followed a ceremony commemorating the 100th anniversary of the first game in franchise history, which came against the Montreal Maroons. Once the puck dropped, the Canadiens dominated for stretches with the puck in the offensive zone. That allowed them to take the lead when Lane Hutson spun around Matt Rempe and put a shot in the perfect place for Phillip Danault to deflect it into the net. Their advantage lasted less than two minutes. With Juraj Slafkovský slow to guard Marcus Pettersson back down the ice, the defenseman banked the puck off Cuylle in the crease to bring life to a fired-up crowd inside Madison Square Garden. Montreal then showed why it ranks second to last in the NHL on the power play despite overflowing with talent from Hutson and Slafkovský to Cole Caufield and Nick Suzuki. When the top unit failed to score, Alex Newhook missing the net paved the way for Cuylle to get a head of steam and beat Jacob Fowler short side off the rush with 56.3 seconds left in the second. Another unsuccessful Canadiens power play in the third was cut short by an interference penalty on Noah Dobson. Scott Morrow scored just his second career goal with 13:16 left. Fowler allowed three goals on 26 shots. At the other end, Joonas Korpisalo made 24 saves to win for the third time in as many starts since missing the first five-plus weeks of the season because of injury. Rangers: Host defending champion Carolina in a Sunday matinee.

On Nov. 16, 2026 at Madison Square Garden, the Rangers hosted the Montreal Canadiens and celebrated with a special pregame ceremony. A night one hundred years in the making pic.twitter.com/YXOKWITeN0 Hosted by legendary broadcaster Sam Rosen, the ceremony gathered former Rangers players and the families of former Rangers players at center ice, standing underneath an enormous centennial banner hanging from the scoreboard. Included in the group was Mark Messier , who helped the Rangers to their Stanley Cup victory in 1994. Messier spoke a few words to the crowd, starting with a quick shoutout to former goalie Henrik Lundqvist for his recent goalie goal at the Rangers Alumni Classic on Sunday. items.body: Register Login Blues Recall Nathan Walker By Brennan McClain | at November 16, 2026 6:01 pm The St. Louis Blues have added some depth as their forward corps recovers from a few minor injuries. According to a team announcement , the Blues recalled forward Nathan Walker from the Springfield Thunderbirds in the AHL. Walker, 32, earns his first call-up of the 2026-27 season after spending the last two years in the NHL. He’s only two years removed from recording his best NHL season, registering eight goals and 16 points in 73 games, while averaging 12:06 of ice time per game. Shortly before the 2025-26 season, the Blues signed Walker to a two-year, $1.78MM ($887.5K AAV) extension through the 2027-28 season. Moving back into a true depth role last season, Walker finished with four goals and 11 points in 46 games, while averaging 11:59 of ice time. Unfortunately, a long-term upper-body injury in December eliminated most of the momentum he had accrued. Leading up to the 2026-27 campaign, the Blues passed Walker through waivers. After clearing waivers in September, Walker began the year with the Thunderbirds, making his first AHL appearance since the 2023-24 season. He’s been relatively productive so far, scoring five goals and six points in 13 games with a -1 rating. Despite the call-up, it’s not a foregone conclusion that Walker will play in St. Louis’ upcoming contest against the Anaheim Ducks tomorrow. The Blues recently suffered injuries to Aleksanteri Kaskimaki and Jake Neighbours , though both are considered day-to-day. Neighbours practiced this morning, so there’s a strong chance he’ll play. However, Walker could have an opportunity if Kaskimaki and Neighbours are ruled out, as game-time decisions.

items.body: Blueshirts legend provides fun moment during exhibition to benefit pediatric cancer care New York Rangers legend Henrik Lundqvist scored a goalie goal at the Alumni Classic at Madison Square Garden on Sunday. Late in the annual event with the opposing net empty, Lundqvist gloved a shot by defenseman Brendan Smith , skated out of the crease to his left and let it fly down the ice. 🚨 WE HAVE A HENRIK LUNDQVIST GOAL 🚨 pic.twitter.com/44jBWQvlze Earlier this season before injury ended his season, Rangers goalie Igor Shesterkin scored a goalie goal to the delight of Lundqvist, who was working as an MSG studio analyst for that game. Over his 15 NHL seasons - all with the Rangers - Lundqvist had a few close calls but never scored a goal. On Sunday, he put so much juice on the shot he fell backward to the ice on the follow through, getting a pretty good look at his retired number up in the rafters of the Garden. When he got up, Lundqvist skated back to his net until he was seemingly coaxed into going for the fist bump line from the bench. Former MSG broadcasters Sam Rosen and Joe Micheletti who were back on the call and enjoyed the feat. The Rangers Alumni Classic is in its fifth season. All proceeds from the event benefited the Garden of Dreams Foundation and Northwell Foundation, resulting in a $270,000 check awarded to the Foundations prior to the game. Prior to the game - which featured over 40 Rangers alumni - Garden of Dreams and Cohen’s Children’s Medical Center patient Paulie Grossman, who is 4-years-old and fighting aplastic anemia, dropped the ceremonial puck between former Rangers captains Ryan Callahan and Mark Messier .

Calgary did not make a corresponding transaction, leaving their roster with 22 players. Calgary recalled Stromgren, 23, on October 30th. He had a phenomenal start, scoring two goals with a +3 rating through his first three games while averaging 9:30 of ice time per game. Unfortunately, his pace has slowed since, as he went scoreless in his following three appearances with a -2 rating, averaging 9:01 per game. The Ornskoldsvik, Sweden, native joined the Flames organization in 2021 when he was selected with the 45th overall pick in the 2021 NHL Draft. During his draft season, MODO Hockey in HockeyAllsvenskan was the highest level he played, scoring three goals and nine points in 27 games. Stromgren didn’t come to North America until the 2022-23 campaign. Since then, he has developed into a quality secondary scorer for the Wranglers. After scoring seven goals and 27 points in 68 AHL contests during the 2023-24 season, Stromgren has registered 28 goals and 107 points in his next 147 appearances. There are some questions regarding his play on defense, but there is hope that Stromgren could develop into a strong middle-six contributor. Now with an open roster spot, the Flames could go in a few different directions. Even though defenseman Kevin Bahl has been ruled out for the rest of the season, Calgary has already filled his roster spot with Brayden Pachal . The Flames recently activated (and reassigned) forward Samuel Honzek from the injured reserve, so he could take Stromgren’s roster spot, assuming his time in the AHL goes well.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect One of the best teams in the NHL will be without one of its veteran depth defensemen for the time being. Olli Maatta of the Minnesota Wild will be sidelined for at least one week with an upper-body injury, according to Wild head coach John Hynes, who shared the update with reporters, including Michael Russo of The Athletic , after the team’s practice on Monday. Maatta, who began his career by quickly earning a pair of Stanley Cup rings with the Pittsburgh Penguins , has become a reliable, experienced journeyman in the second half of his career. The 32-year-old is in his first year in St. Paul after coming over from Calgary as part of the deal that sent Jacob Middleton to the Flames and also brought Blake Coleman to the Wild. Through 18 appearances, Maatta has six points on a goal and five assists while skating to a plus-11 rating on an average of 19:16 of time on ice per game. Recently, Maatta has been playing alongside Zach Bogosian on the Wild’s bottom pairing. Matt Kiersted, a Minnesota native, will draw into the lineup on Tuesday in the veteran Finn’s absence. The Wild have been one of the hottest teams in the NHL all season long to this point, and their 15-3-4 record is good enough to give them a seven-point lead over the Colorado Avalanche and Nashville Predators , meaning they’ve opened up a sizable lead in what was supposed to be an incredibly competitive division. Minnesota has gone 8-0-2 in its past 10 games, and it will look to keep its lengthy point streak going on Tuesday night when the Predators pay a visit to Grand Casino Arena. The Wild will then kick off a road trip and will close out their slate for the week by visiting the Calgary Flames Thursday and the Vancouver Canucks on Saturday.

items.title: Jagr hopes to host farewell hockey game next summer
items.summary: Jaromir Jagr hasn't announced his retirement, but he could host a farewell hockey game in his native Czechia next summer.
items.body: 54-year-old forward hasn’t played in 11 months, has ‘no obligation’ to officially announce retirement Jaromir Jagr hasn't announced his retirement, but he could host a farewell hockey game in his native Czechia next summer. The 54-year-old hockey legend has not played a game since Dec. 21, 2025, with Kladno in the Czech Extraliga. "Truth is, I have something in mind," the forward told Czech newspaper Deník Sport in a story published Monday to promote his autobiography, "JA68," and a special line of trading cards. "I'm not sure if people would be interested. But if it were to happen, the ideal date would be around the beginning of August 2027. There will be the World Cup (of Hockey) in Prague during the season after that, but I am not sure I would be able to skate at that time." The game could be similar to the one Zdeno Chara hosted Aug. 21 in Trencin, Slovakia. Several of the 49-year-old’s friends and former teammates participated, including Jagr, Boston Bruins forward David Pastrnak , and fellow Hockey Hall of Famers Ray Bourque , Mark Recchi , Marian Hossa and Patrice Bergeron . "I would like to bring in some really high-quality players," Jagr said. "Former teammates, but also players who are still active, to make sure the game is played at a high level. I don't want people to watch a bunch of old guys struggling to get around the ice. I would also be happy if other players who never got the chance to have a proper farewell could have one too. There are quite a few from our generation who fall into that category, and they definitely deserve it as well." items.title: Jets’ Scheifele leads NHL’s three stars after setting franchise scoring record
items.summary: Winnipeg Jets centre Mark Scheifele, Minnesota Wild goaltender Jesper Wallstedt and Carolina Hurricanes left-wing Nikolaj Ehlers have been named the NHL’s three stars of the week.
items.body: Winnipeg Jets centre Mark Scheifele , Minnesota Wild goaltender Jesper Wallstedt and Carolina Hurricanes left-wing Nikolaj Ehlers have been named the NHL's three stars of the week. Scheifele led the league with three goals and five assists in three games as the Jets extended their winning streak to six contests. The 33-year-old Scheifele now has 933 points (379 goals, 554 assists), surpassing the old franchise record of 929 set by Dale Hawerchuk in 1990. He also moved past Thomas Steen for the franchise assists record and tied Hawerchuk for the Jets' goals mark. Wallstedt went 3-0-0 with a 1.66 goals-against average and .944 save percentage to backstop the Central Division-leading Wild to a perfect three-game road trip. The 24-year-old tops the NHL with 14 wins through 19 appearances this season and is 8-0-1 in his last nine starts dating to Oct. 24. Ehlers had a goal and four assists across two games at the NHL Global Series in Finland, where the Eastern Conference-leading Hurricanes swept a two-game series against the Seattle Kraken.

items.title: Oilers activate Isaac Howard, loan him to AHL Bakersfield
items.body: The 22-year-old forward has been activated from injured reserve and loaned to the AHL's Bakersfield Condors, the Edmonton Oilers announced on Monday. Howard left the Oilers' Oct. 31 win over the New York Islanders following a knee-on-knee collision. After the game, head coach Mike Babcock did not seem too worried about the injury and said he expected Howard to miss a couple of weeks. His return to play is on par with that prediction. Howard has one goal and two assists in 13 games in his second season in the league. He is averaging 8:53 minutes of ice time.
